relevance_note: Family case report: "The proband, his daughter, and his sister who are all affected with chronic urticaria and angioedema each carry the c.65G>A (p.R22Q) variant inTNFAIP3."
method_note: Hand-built from a full read of a short case report (no tables); a small Python script assembled the JSON and checked spans. Labels: the proband has no paper label, so 'patient' (rule 5); relatives by rule 2 ('sister of patient', 'daughter of patient', 'mother of patient'). The proband's father is mentioned only as deceased and untested, so he gets no row. The mother is in scope as a relative tested negative for the TNFAIP3 variant; she carries the GJB2 variant, recorded as an other-gene variant row (also for the proband). Sister and daughter were stated not to carry the GJB2 variant (no rows for absent variants). The GJB2 variant is printed as 'c.35del' in Results and 'c.35delG' in the Conclusion; recorded as c.35del with NM_004004.5. The paper says reads were aligned to GRCh37/hg19 but prints GRCh38 coordinates; recorded as printed. TNFAIP3 variant_type 'missense' is from the title, which names this variant. Zygosity for the proband from 'heterozygous ... in all affected members'. Daughter's inheritance recorded 'inherited paternal' because her father (the proband) carries the same variant (D-24); her mother is not mentioned. Sister's inheritance left not reported: the paper does not state that the tested mother is also the sister's mother. Proband's TNFAIP3 inheritance not reported (mother negative, father deceased untested). In silico predictions and molecular modelling are computational, not functional assays, so functional_evidence_statement is not reported; the authors state functional analyses are still needed. Normal findings (bone marrow biopsy, CBC, mast cell panel, TSH, serum protein electrophoresis) recorded as excluded abnormalities of what each test names; the normal CBC was not used to exclude the checklist item 'cytopenia (autoimmune)'. Checklist: urticaria/hives recorded as 'skin lesions' observed; fever during recurrent attacks every two weeks recorded as 'recurrent fever' observed for the proband. The elevated anti-IgE receptor antibody was not mapped to the 'autoantibodies' checklist item because the paper does not call it an autoantibody. Diarrhea during attacks was not mapped to 'gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation'. The mother's 'unaffected' status is recorded as chronic urticaria and angioedema excluded, from 'who is unaffected' read with the preceding sentence naming the affected members' disease. No contradictions about phenotypes found.
